why: Commit 1 only adds measuring cases, but commits 2 and 3 are made or skipped on the measured figures and then change money paths: rewriting checkout's per-line insert loop into one multi-row insert needs a judgement of whether later per-line work (stock holds, bookings, gift cards) depends on the line being written first, and gating order triggers needs choosing which trigger functions count as optional-feature ones from their SQL bodies and rewriting them in a migration CI applies to production. The brief itself says 'if you cannot tell, stop', which is where the cheap model does worst.
harm_if_wrong: Order lines matched to the wrong ids or stock held in the wrong order at checkout, or a replaced trigger that stops writing bonus credit, gift card or affiliate rows for stores that have the feature on.
make_it_cheaper: End the step after commit 1 with the measured figures handed back, and write commits 2 and 3 as separate briefs naming the exact loop changes and the trigger functions to gate once the numbers are known.
brief_problems: Commit 1 names src/server/shop-journey.int.test.ts as the file to extend, but step 1.12's brief puts the placed-order and visit measurement in src/server/order-writes.int.test.ts; the rg finder may pick either.
Case 3 uses `set local track_functions = 'all'`, a superuser-only setting; whether the integration database's role may set it is not checked.
The decision row instruction uses 'tail -1' on unsorted ids, unlike the other briefs' sort -n.
